audience.text: Python developers building 3D content pipelines, especially in 3D printing, CAD visualization, and web 3D asset preparation workflows.

capabilities.text: Imports OBJ, STL, glTF/GLB, COLLADA, and 3MF files through Scene.open() with automatic format detection from file extension or explicit FileFormat.
capabilities.title: Load multiple 3D formats

capabilities.text: Exports scenes to OBJ, STL, glTF/GLB, and 3MF using Scene.save() with format-specific options for compression, coordinate system flipping, and unit scaling.
capabilities.title: Export scenes to common formats

capabilities.text: Construct hierarchical scene graphs using Scene.root_node, Node.create_child_node(), and Node.child_nodes, with independent Transform per node.
capabilities.title: Build and traverse scene graphs

capabilities.text: Create meshes from control points and polygons, or convert primitives to meshes, then edit geometry via Mesh.control_points and Mesh.polygons.
capabilities.title: Construct and edit mesh geometry

capabilities.text: Attach LambertMaterial, PhongMaterial, or PbrMaterial to nodes and set diffuse, specular, albedo, metallic, and roughness properties directly.
capabilities.title: Assign and configure materials

capabilities.text: Build keyframe animations using AnimationClip, AnimationNode, and KeyframeSequence, and store skeletal bind-pose data with Pose and related types.
capabilities.title: Support keyframe animation

limitations.text: FBX export is not implemented: FbxExporter.save() and save_to_stream() raise NotImplementedError.
COLLADA export is not reachable through Scene.save() due to exporter lookup order issues.
Scene.render() and the entire aspose.threed.render module raise NotImplementedError.
Texture and TextureBase raise NotImplementedError on construction, so image-backed textures cannot be created.
Mesh boolean operations (union, difference, intersect) raise NotImplementedError.
NURBS curve evaluation and surface-to-mesh conversion raise NotImplementedError.

problems_solved.text: Enables programmatic 3D scene manipulation using a pure-Python API without requiring external native SDKs or runtime dependencies.
Supports common 3D file formats used in additive manufacturing and web 3D pipelines, including OBJ, STL, glTF/GLB, COLLADA, and 3MF.
Provides parameterized primitives and direct mesh construction for authoring geometry from scratch.

product_summary.text: Aspose.3D FOSS for Python is a pure-Python, MIT-licensed library for loading, constructing, and exporting 3D scenes without native dependencies.

uncertainties: The exact set of formats supported beyond those explicitly listed in format:input.* and format:output.* facts is unclear; the README mentions FBX import but facts do not confirm it.
Whether the library supports animation import beyond keyframe construction is not confirmed by facts.
The behavior of Scene.save() when passed a stream without a filename and without explicit FileFormat is not fully documented in facts.

workflows.name: Import and inspect 3D scenes
workflows.text: Load OBJ, STL, glTF, COLLADA, or 3MF files using Scene.open() and inspect the resulting node graph, entities, and materials.

workflows.name: Export scenes to target formats
workflows.text: Write scenes to OBJ, STL, glTF/GLB, or 3MF using Scene.save() with format-specific SaveOptions for compression, coordinate flipping, and unit scaling.

workflows.name: Build scenes from primitives
workflows.text: Construct parameterized primitives like Box, Sphere, Cylinder, and Dish, then convert them to editable meshes using to_mesh().

workflows.name: Construct meshes from control points
workflows.text: Create meshes vertex by vertex using Mesh.control_points and Mesh.create_polygon(), then attach materials and save to target formats.

workflows.name: Assign materials to nodes
workflows.text: Attach LambertMaterial, PhongMaterial, or PbrMaterial to nodes and configure diffuse, specular, albedo, metallic, and roughness properties.

workflows.name: Triangulate polygon meshes
workflows.text: Triangulate arbitrary polygon data using PolygonModifier.triangulate() with a real ear-clipping implementation.
